content.intro: Learn diagnosing file and asset problems through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Diagnosing File and Asset Problems matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines diagnosing file and asset problems as part of static files, media, and file storage. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Static files returning 404; Broken media URLs; Incorrect storage configuration; File permission problems; Deployment and CDN caching issues. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Static files returning 404
items.text: For Static files returning 404, identify the Django component responsible, the inputs and outputs it owns, and the boundary conditions that matter. Use the accompanying example as a starting point, verify it with the official versioned documentation, and record one test demonstrating expected behavior.

items.title: Broken media URLs
items.text: Broken media URLs is part of the request/response contract. Match routes and methods explicitly, return an appropriate response/status, and test success, missing-resource and unauthorized paths.

items.title: Incorrect storage configuration
items.text: Configuration for Incorrect storage configuration should be explicit, environment-aware, and validated before serving requests. Record defaults and deploy-specific values, keep secrets outside committed content, and test the setting that changes behavior.

items.title: File permission problems
items.text: File permission problems is a server-side responsibility where applicable. Define who may perform the action and on which object, validate untrusted input, test denied cases, and document sensitive-data handling.

items.title: Deployment and CDN caching issues
items.text: Deployment and CDN caching issues should be planned for the actual hosting topology: configuration, permissions, resource limits, observability, rollback/recovery and a testable operating procedure all matter.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Diagnosing File and Asset Problems
content_blocks.code:
from django.urls import path
from . import views

urlpatterns = [
    path("items/<int:item_id>/", views.item_detail, name="item-detail"),
]
content_blocks.expected_output: The route converter passes an integer item_id to the named view.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Open a local project using the documented Django 6.1-compatible Python environment. If this snippet depends on model names, URL configuration, settings, or an optional package, add those prerequisites before running it. Otherwise inspect it as a static example. CodeLeaf browser preview does not execute Django/Python server code.
content_blocks.troubleshooting: The view and project include() wiring must exist; URL conversion does not perform authorization or database lookup.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.
